facts.statement: Domeykodactylus lived during the Early Cretaceous in the Santa Ana Formation of Antofagasta, Chile.
facts.quote: Domeykodactylus is an extinct genus of dsungaripterid pterosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Berriasian-Albian)-age Santa Ana Formation at Quebrada de la Carreta in Antofagasta, Chile.

facts.statement: The genus Domeykodactylus was named in 2000 by David Martill, Eberhard Frey, Guillermo Chong Diaz, and Charles Michael Bell.
facts.quote: The genus was named in 2000 by David Martill, Eberhard Frey, Guillermo Chong Diaz and Charles Michael Bell.

facts.statement: The genus name combines the Cordillera Domeyko and the Greek word for 'finger' to reference the long wing finger typical of pterosaurs.
facts.quote: The genus name is derived from the Cordillera Domeyko and Greek daktylos, "finger" in reference to the wing finger typical of pterosaurs.

facts.statement: The species name ceciliae honors geologist Cecilia Demargasso for her collaboration with the researchers.
facts.quote: The specific name honors geologist Cecilia Demargasso of the Universidad Católica del Norte, "who was so kind to us".

facts.statement: The fossil material was initially mistaken for belonging to the genus Pterodaustro.
facts.quote: The fossil had at first been thought to belong to Pterodaustro.

facts.statement: Domeykodactylus possessed a crest running along the top of its premaxilla.
facts.quote: Domeykodactylus had a crest running along the top of the premaxilla.

facts.statement: The crest was made of vertical trabeculae that were originally confused with the filter teeth of Pterodaustro.
facts.quote: The bone structure of the crest consists of vertical trabeculae, narrow struts; it was this texture that had originally been mistaken for the fine filter teeth of Pterodaustro.

facts.statement: Each dentary bone contained sixteen tooth sockets, though the teeth themselves are missing.
facts.quote: There are sixteen tooth sockets, from which the teeth themselves have been lost, in each dentary.

facts.statement: The skull was estimated to be 30 cm long and the wingspan was 2 meters.
facts.quote: The skull length has been estimated at 30 cm and the wingspan at 2 meter (6.6 ft).

facts.statement: Domeykodactylus was assigned to the Dsungaripteridae family due to its elevated tooth sockets.
facts.quote: because of the elevated tooth sockets it was assigned to the latter group.

facts.statement: Domeykodactylus lived between 143.1 and 100.5 million years ago, from the Berriasian to the Albian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Berriasian to Albian (143.1 to 100.5 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Domeykodactylus was the first published example of a dsungaripterid found in South America, whereas most other family members are from Asia.
rejected.quote: It was the first published example of a dsungaripterid in South America, most other members of the family being from Asia.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'was the first published example of a dsungaripterid'
